title: Preflight security scrapbook: SOC2 scoping notes
body:
Purpose / form factor
- Quick personal notebook for preflight scoping of SOC2 (security + availability focus). Not polished, not shareable as-is.
- Use for triage before I formalize evidence matrix in Confluence.

High level goals
- Decide minimal scope for first attestation: hosted API + control plane, exclude customer-managed private nodes for now? (pros: smaller blast radius, cons: sales asks)
- Identify 6–8 candidate controls we can realistically evidence in 6–8 weeks.
- Draft list of owners and quick evidence sources to hand off to auditors.

Scope questions (need answers)
- Include Dedicated vs Hosted: do we treat Dedicated as part of Redwood org controls or as customer-segregated? Need legal input.
- Private deployments (on-prem/VPC): if we ship software to customer infra, likely out of scope for our org controls — confirm with audit lead.
- Which cloud accounts map to prod? (list: redwood-prod-us-east, redwood-prod-eu, redwood-controlplane) — verify with infra.

Initial control candidates + evidence sketch
1) Access management (IAM / SSO)
   - Evidence: Okta org settings export, SAML metadata, list of admins, provisioning/deprovisioning runbook, last 6 months deprovision events (Jira/HR tickets).
   - Quick check: run Okta admin reports + snapshot of SCIM connector logs (ask identity team).
2) Logging & monitoring (detection)
   - Evidence: CloudTrail / Audit Logs bucket (s3://redwood-audit/), retention policy doc, CloudWatch alert configs, Datadog dashboards, example incident alert history.
   - Quick query: `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-audit/ --recursive --human-readable --summarize | head`
3) Change management (deploys + approvals)
   - Evidence: GitHub protected branch settings, PR review policy, Jenkins/Spinnaker release notes, rollout runbook, sample canary rollback.
4) Patch management (OS + dependency)
   - Evidence: AMI rebuild schedule, vuln scan reports (Trivy/Anchore), package update ticket history.
5) Backup & restore (stateful components)
   - Evidence: RDS snapshot schedule, backup verification runbook, restore exercise log (last 12 months).
6) Incident response
   - Evidence: IR runbook, postmortem examples, PagerDuty rotation, mean time to acknowledge metrics.
7) Data encryption (at rest + in transit)
   - Evidence: KMS key policies, TLS cert inventory, HSM/KMS integration diagrams for private customers.
8) Service availability / capacity planning
   - Evidence: SLA docs, Dedicated autoscale config, capacity test report (load test results), runbook for failover.

Evidence inventory — rough mapping (very rough)
- Okta exports -> identity team
- s3://redwood-audit -> infra ops
- RDS snapshots -> infra ops / storage
- GitHub branch protection -> devplatform
- Datadog dashboards + alert history -> observability team
- Patch/vuln scans -> platform-security
- Backup verify logs -> storage/infra

Control owner hypotheses (assignments to confirm)
- Identity: Jamal Rivera
- Logging/Monitoring: Priya Desai
- Deploy/change mgmt: Release eng lead (TBD)
- Patching: Platform eng (Sahil?)
- Backup: Infra ops (Elena)
- IR: SRE / Security (Marta / Jamal)
- Crypto: Security (me + cryptogroup)

Open & sticky questions (to unblock quickly)
- How do we treat Dedicated customers who purchase a dedicated GPU pool but still depend on our control plane? Auditor may expect control over that plane only; need narrative.
- Evidence retention: auditors often want 12 months. Do we have that in logs? If not, what's the plan?
- Where are legal/regulatory exceptions documented? (Link missing)

Quick tickets to create (prio order)
- SEC-Create: list of prod accounts and owners (assign to infra)
- SEC-Evidence: export Okta admin logs for last 12 months (identity)
- SEC-Infra: confirm CloudTrail retention and lifecycle to secure long-term storage (infra ops)
- SEC-IR: select 3 postmortems to redact and present as example evidence (SRE + security)

Small artifacts to draft now (in parallel)
- Short narrative: "What we own/what customers own" (1 page) — give to auditor to avoid scope creep.
- Evidence matrix template (CSV) with columns: control, owner, evidence path, retention, confidence, action required.
- FAQ: Dedicated vs Private customer implications (for sales/AMs).

Possible quick wins (low effort, high value)
- Snapshot Okta admin list & last login stats (1 hour)
- Export 3 months of CloudTrail and confirm lifecycle (2–4 hours)
- Produce sample redacted postmortem (3–6 hours)

Timeline idea (very rough)
- Week 0–1: scope decision + account inventory + owners assigned
- Week 2–4: collect evidence for top 4 controls
- Week 5–6: fix minor gaps + produce narratives + auditor dry-run

Notes to self / reminders
- Don’t forget to ask infra about the separate billing/projects for Dedicated pools — might create multiple prod accounts we need to list.
- Check with legal on non-disclosure clauses for private/on-prem customers if asked for evidence.
- When talking to auditors, emphasize runtime isolation features (KV cache, controlled fallbacks) only as system design, not as control evidence unless we have logs.

Raw scratch ideas (one-liners)
- Could we produce a "SOC2 bootstrap" package: top-4 controls + evidence + contact list + 1-pg org narrative? That would help sales and reduce audit churn.
- Consider flagging Dedicated customers in our CMDB to simplify scope mapping.

Next steps (this doc)
- Convert this into Confluence evidence matrix template (deadline: 2026-03-05).
- Ping owners listed above to confirm.
- Create the 4 Jira tickets noted under Quick tickets.

End of scratchpad. Will clean up shortly and link from main SOC2 page.

---
Meta: created quick during hallway convo w/ Jamal — some assumptions likely wrong; verify before sharing.
